correctness.rationale: Finite Blaschke expansion gives identical initial Taylor data and degree-M difference -(1-a²). Uniform generalized-binomial convergence for |lambda|<1/2 allows coefficient-wise integration; unequal index (j,k) probes inner coefficients only through min(j,k). Thus all orders <=2M coincide and exactly (M,M+1) and its conjugate produce a nonzero first difference -2(1-a²)beta_M beta_(M+1). Independently reproduced with exact rational polynomial coefficient enumeration in 72 triples; finite tests are only corroboration.

value.rationale: A motivated sharp boundary for nonlinear Hardy polynomial approximation: for every non-even exponent a complete trial-polynomial objective cannot be reduced to any finite inner Taylor jet, even among finite Blaschke products. The exact 2M+1 onset quantifies how high inner coefficients enter and complements finite-jet sufficiency at even powers. It does not confuse objective sensitivity with optimal-solution sensitivity.
